item.title: Maine couple forced to choose food or heat as oil prices skyrocket
item.description: Along with diesel and gas, the price of heating oil is up, and no state depends on it more than Maine. Meg Oliver spoke with residents there, now forced to make some tough decisions.

item.title: Vance says "selling access to the White House" is "disgusting"
item.description: Vice President JD Vance told CBS News in a "Things That Matter" town hall in Michigan that anybody who is "selling access to the White House" should "suffer consequences."

item.title: 3 children, 1 adult killed in Oregon school shooting, sources say
item.description: At least four people were killed in Thursday's shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School, multiple law enforcement sources told CBS News. The suspect is also dead.

item.title: New book explores sonic attacks on American diplomats known as "Havana Syndrome"
item.description: A new book, "The Havana Syndrome," investigates the alleged sonic attacks against American diplomats overseas that left many with symptoms including insomnia and memory loss. Co-authors Oriana Zill de Granados and Michael Ray share more details.

item.title: Cornell's president grilled by faculty over handling of former student's gang rape allegations
item.description: The president of Cornell University faced intense scrutiny from faculty members for his handling of allegations of gang rape that occurred at a fraternity house in 2024. Lilia Luciano reports on Wednesday's faculty senate meeting.

item.title: Michigan Senate contest earns outsized attention from Trump
item.description: Democrats hold the Michigan Senate seat on the ballot this fall, and Republican Mike Rogers is trying to pick it up for the Republicans. Ed O'Keefe has more details on the race and the latest on the Trump administration.

item.title: Is Texas' Senate race a perfect storm for Democrats?
item.description: The latest Texas Senate race polls show Democrat James Talarico with a slight edge over Republican Ken Paxton. Political strategists Chuck Rocha and Erin Maguire join "The Takeout" with analysis.

item.title: Oregon elementary school shooter was a 16-year-old male, sources say
item.description: Law enforcement sources tell CBS News that at least three children and one adult are dead after a shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday. The shooter, whom sources say was a 16-year-old male, is also dead. CBS News senior crime reporter Anna Schecter has the latest.

item.title: Vance talks economy, inflation and corruption in CBS News town hall
item.description: Vice President JD Vance sat down with "CBS Evening News" anchor Tony Dokoupil in Michigan for a "Things that Matter" town hall during his midterm campaign blitz.

item.title: Feds probing suspicious letters to election officials, lawmakers
item.description: Federal investigators said they are looking into suspicious letters containing unknown substances that were mailed to state election officials and congressional offices.

item.title: Several killed, including children, in Oregon elementary school shooting, sources say
item.description: Police say a gunman walked into Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday and opened fire. Law enforcement sources said that at least four people are dead, including children. The suspect is also dead. Mark Strassmann reports.

item.title: Wasserman Schultz says she thinks Florida GOP's redistricting will "end up a big fat dummymander"
item.description: Florida's newly redrawn 20th Congressional District will soon elect its first non-African-American representative since 1992. The Democratic nominee, Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz, joins to discuss her party's chances in the state.

item.title: 3 children, 1 adult killed in Oregon elementary school shooting, sources say
item.description: New details are emerging in Thursday's shooting at a Bend, Oregon, elementary school with sources saying three children and one adult were killed. The suspected shooter is also dead. Felipe Rodriguez, adjunct professor at the John Jay College of Criminal Justice, joins "The Daily Report" to explain what happens next.

item.title: Vance says he would comply with Democrat-led corruption probe amid Guilfoyle's firing
item.description: Vice President JD Vance addressed public concerns with corruption within the Trump administration at a CBS News town hall Thursday, just 19 days ahead of the midterms. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports.

item.title: Pennsylvania man who killed 8 people was "controlling" patriarch, police say
item.description: The Pennsylvania man accused of killing eight people "exercised significant control" over his family at their Erie home, police said.

item.title: Pentagon may use "mother of all bombs" on Iran, sources say
item.description: The White House is preparing plans to use a weapon dubbed the "mother of all bombs" on Iran, sources say. CBS News' James LaPorta has more on that and his report that former Army Chief of Staff Randy George warned months before the Iran war of a U.S. missile defense shortage, according to sources.

item.title: Sikh separatist says FBI warned him of new threat against him
item.description: Gurpatwant Singh Pannun told CBS News that the FBI visited his home to warn him about what he said was an "imminent threat to my life."

item.title: Michigan GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers says he's "not a big fan" of Trump's Russian diesel deal
item.description: Vice President JD Vance is campaigning for Republican Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers on Thursday night. CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe spoke with Rogers ahead of the event.

item.title: Multiple people, including children, killed in Oregon elementary school shooting
item.description: Authorities are investigating a shooting at an Oregon elementary school. Multiple people, including children, were killed, sources say. The suspected shooter is also dead. CBS News crime reporter Anna Schecter has more details.

item.title: Talarico defends abortion stance at CNN town hall
item.description: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico appeared on CNN for a town hall Wednesday night and tried to quell doubts about his support for capitalism and immigration enforcement. He also spoke about his position on abortion. CBS News congressional correspondent Caitlin Huey-Burns has more. CNN is owned by CBS News' parent company, Skydance.

item.title: U.S. sending hundreds of troops to Latin America for training, New York Times reports
item.description: The U.S. will send several hundred Army soldiers to train and conduct exercises with Latin American military forces, The New York Times reports. Officials said it is part of an effort to fight drug trafficking in the region. Eric Schmitt, senior national security correspondent for The New York Times, joins CBS News to discuss his story.

item.title: Justice Dept. sues California, claims noncitizens were sent ballots
item.description: The Justice Department sued California, alleging that the federal government has identified more than 20,000 noncitizens who are unlawfully registered to vote.

item.title: Children injured, suspect dead after Oregon elementary school shooting
item.description: A suspect is dead after a shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday. CBS News' Jericka Duncan anchors a special report.

item.title: Vance says selling access to White House is disgusting and despicable
item.description: Vice President JD Vance tells Tony Dokoupil he thinks if someone's selling access to the White House, "That's disgusting and despicable and they should suffer consequences." See more of the conversation, Saturday at 8 p.m. ET on CBS.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz still unsafe for ships, maritime group warns
item.description: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz still face "indiscriminate attacks" even if they switch off tracking systems, a maritime risk firm warns.

item.title: The safety questions facing America's roller coasters
item.description: A deadly incident at Six Flags in Georgia is raising new questions about roller coaster safety. Experts say inconsistent safety standards and a so-called roller coaster loophole limit federal oversight of amusement park rides. Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: Kristi Noem no longer serving as Trump envoy to Shield of the Americas
item.description: Former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem is no longer serving as the Trump administration's envoy to the Shield of the Americas initiative, a State Department official said.

item.title: Judge finds Musk, Noem targeted ex-FEMA official
item.description: A federal magistrate judge said Elon Musk and former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem knowingly spread false information about Mary Comans, the former CFO of FEMA.

item.title: As Jolly runs for Florida gov., he confronts prior ties to alleged fraudster
item.description: Shortly after David Jolly launched his campaign for Florida governor, his former boss was indicted for taking over $100 million from a disability nonprofit. Jolly says he wasn't aware of the scheme.

item.title: Six Flags closes 9 rides across 6 parks after deadly incident
item.description: Six Flags has temporarily closed rides similar to Goliath, the roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia from which a man fell.
